office_does: Cowlitz County District Court judges hear misdemeanor and gross misdemeanor criminal cases and some civil matters county-wide.
race_blurb: Open seat: two Longview prosecutors who sit as pro tem judges, Christopher Eastwood (nearly two decades as prosecutor, defender and civil lawyer) and Nicole Knowles (nine years of Cowlitz prosecution, founder of the city's therapeutic court).

candidates.summary: Longview attorney and District Court pro tem judge since 2022, with nearly two decades as a prosecutor, public defender and civil litigator.
highlights: Former Kelso and Longview city prosecutor, Cowlitz County public defender and Thurston County deputy prosecutor [S2]
Pro tem judge in Cowlitz County District Court since 2022 [S1]
Taught First Amendment law as an adjunct at Gonzaga Law School [S1][S2]
Pledges to 'protect constitutional rights, and bring accountability with compassion' [S1]

experience.basis: Runs on nearly two decades of practice and four years as a pro tem judge; not an incumbent.

safety.basis: Balanced professional formation: prosecutor, public defender and civil litigator.

candidates.summary: Lead prosecutor for the City of Longview and District Court pro tem judge, formerly the county's child-abuse prosecutor, who helped found the Cowlitz Municipal Therapeutic Court.
highlights: Five years as Cowlitz County's senior deputy prosecutor for child sexual abuse cases [S1][S3]
Helped create the Cowlitz Municipal Therapeutic Court in 2024 for addiction and mental health cases [S1][S3]
Endorsed by Presiding Superior Court Judge Patricia Fassett and other local judges [S4]
Chosen for appointment by 83.3% of respondents in a 2026 judicial evaluation poll [S5]

experience.basis: Runs on nine years of local prosecution, pro tem service and broad endorsements from the local bench; not an incumbent.

safety.basis: Professional formation entirely in prosecution, tempered by founding a treatment-based therapeutic court.
